html:
Søren Kierkegaard was a Danish philosopher and religious writer from Copenhagen, often called the father of existentialism.

He wrote many of his books under false names, so that each voice could argue its own view of life. In Either/Or, Fear and Trembling and The Sickness unto Death he wrote about anxiety, despair and choice, and about faith as a leap that reason cannot make for you. He held that truth is found in how a single person lives, not in a system like Hegel's.

At the end of his life he attacked the comfortable Danish state church. He died at 42, little read outside Denmark. In the 1900s German and French thinkers took him up, and he shaped existentialism and modern theology. He was a contemporary of Hans Christian Andersen.
sum: Søren Kierkegaard was a Danish philosopher and religious writer from Copenhagen, often called the father of existentialism.
